summary.title: Implementing a Key-Value Store
summary.one_liner: This table of contents for the IKVS series shows how to build a key-value store from scratch, covering existing store architectures, API design, hash tables, SSD-optimized data structures, and the KingDB project.
takeaways: Key-value stores are compared with relational databases, and the reasons for implementing one are laid out.
Existing stores Kyoto Cabinet and LevelDB are analyzed architecturally and by code review to serve as models.
Open-addressing hash tables are examined with defined metrics and an experimental protocol.
Data structures and file I/O are discussed with SSD performance in mind.
The series covers KingDB's API design, data format, memory management, and a benchmark against Nginx.
summary.summary: This is the main table of contents for a multi-part article series on implementing a key-value store in C/C++. It lists planned parts covering key-value store fundamentals, analysis of Kyoto Cabinet and LevelDB architectures, public API design, hash table implementations, open-addressing hash tables with experiments, and optimizing data structures for SSDs. Later parts cover the data format and memory management of KingDB and a networking comparison between KingServer and Nginx. The page notes that the series is ongoing and the KingDB store has been released at kingdb.org.
